title: Implement quantization profile schema + artifact storage in model registry
creator: Mateo Alvarez
description:
Context
- Quantization Profile Library requires a versioned, signed, hardware-scoped artifact in the model registry.
- Runtime (ENG-18437) and route controls (ENG-18451) depend on stable storage layout + server-side validation to prevent mis-scoped / incompatible profiles from being published.

Scope
1) Define and implement:
   - Quantization profile metadata types (canonical JSON representation + internal typed model)
   - Artifact layout conventions in the model registry
   - Profile manifest format (files, checksums, compatibility constraints)
   - Server-side publish validation (schema + constraints + permissions)
2) Add publish endpoints (internal-only for v1) with audit logging hooks.
3) Document the conventions so runtime and eval harness can resolve + attach results to the right profile version.

Non-goals (v1)
- User-supplied profile uploads outside Redwood-published flows.
- Auto-generation of profiles for all models.

Design / Decisions
- Profiles are immutable once published for a given (profile_id, version). If a fix is needed, publish a new version.
- Versions follow semver, enforced server-side:
  - PATCH: metadata-only changes allowed (docs/notes, adding additional benchmark attachments) with NO changes to weight transform or kernel requirements.
  - MINOR: new hardware scopes or new calibrated artifacts for additional sequence-length regimes, must remain backward-compatible for existing scopes.
  - MAJOR: breaking schema changes or materially different quantization method.
- Hardware scoping is explicit; profiles must declare an allowlist of GPU architectures / SKUs (e.g., sm80, sm90) and supported runtime/kernel families.
- Artifact integrity:
  - Each manifest contains sha256 for every referenced blob.
  - Registry enforces signature verification for manifests using Redwood keyring.
  - Publish endpoint requires “quantization_profile_publisher” permission (restricted to Applied ML + registry maintainers).

Proposed storage layout (implemented)
- Base prefix: registry://quant-profiles/
- Layout:
  - registry://quant-profiles/{model_slug}/{profile_id}/{version}/manifest.json
  - registry://quant-profiles/{model_slug}/{profile_id}/{version}/artifacts/{artifact_name}
  - registry://quant-profiles/{model_slug}/{profile_id}/{version}/reports/{eval_or_perf_report_name}
- manifest.json includes:
  - profile_id, version, model_slug, created_at, created_by
  - quantization_method (fp16/bf16/int8/int4 + algorithm)
  - calibration_notes + calibration_dataset_ref (optional but recommended)
  - hardware_scopes[] (gpu_arch, optional sku allowlist, driver/runtime min)
  - kernel_constraints[] (kernel family, min runtime version, known incompatibilities)
  - sequence_length_regimes[] (e.g., short/medium/long) with per-regime artifact pointers
  - expected_deltas (throughput, p50/p95 latency, cost_per_1k_tokens) as informative-only
  - files[] with uri + sha256 + size_bytes
  - signature (detached or inline per threat model)

Server-side validation rules (implemented)
- Schema validation (required fields + types), hard-fail on unknown top-level fields unless explicitly version-gated.
- Semantic constraints:
  - profile_id must match naming: qp_{model_slug}_{method}_{variant} (enforced prefix + character set).
  - version must be semver and monotonic per (model_slug, profile_id).
  - hardware_scopes must not be empty.
  - For each sequence_length_regime, referenced artifact must exist and be listed in files[] with sha256.
  - Kernel constraints must be satisfiable (e.g., runtime_min <= current supported registry/runtime compatibility table).
- Security constraints:
  - Reject unsigned manifests.
  - Reject manifests signed by unknown key id.
  - Enforce publish permission + record principal in audit log.

Endpoints
- POST /internal/model-registry/quantization-profiles:publish
  - Supports dry_run=true (validation only)
  - Returns canonical profile identifier + resolved artifact URIs
- GET /internal/model-registry/quantization-profiles/{model_slug}/{profile_id}/{version}
  - Used by runtime fetch path + tooling

Acceptance criteria
- A quantization profile can be published to staging registry with:
  - Signed manifest
  - At least one hardware scope
  - At least one sequence-length regime with artifact pointers
- Invalid / mis-scoped profiles are rejected with actionable errors (field path + reason).
- Runtime can resolve the manifest + download artifacts by URI without knowing bucket details.
- Audit log includes who published what (profile_id, version) and from which CI principal.

Test plan
- Unit tests:
  - schema roundtrip and rejection of unknown fields
  - semver monotonicity and immutability rules
  - signature verification (valid/invalid/unknown key)
- Integration tests (staging):
  - publish dry-run and publish commit
  - list/get endpoints
  - attempt publish without permission (403)

Rollout
- Deploy to staging registry first, enable publish endpoint only for CI service account + registry maintainers.
- After successful runtime fetch integration (ENG-18437), enable prod endpoint for Applied ML publishing group.

Links / Implementation
- Registry artifact layout + manifest: sources/github/redwood-model-registry/pr_912_add_profile_artifact_layout_and_manifest.json
- Registry publish API + permission checks: sources/github/redwood-model-registry/pr_931_publish_api_for_quantization_profiles.json
- Core types + JSON schema validation scaffolding in runtime repo: sources/github/redwood/pr_28741_add_quantization_profile_types_and_validation.json

Notes
- This issue intentionally does not define route-level policy schema; see ENG-18451.
- Quality gating is handled by eval harness and approval workflow; see confluence quality gates doc + ENG-18488.
comments: 2025-10-22 — Mateo Alvarez (creator): This is the blocker for runtime resolution work. We need a registry layout that can survive v1->v2 changes without breaking consumers. Please keep manifest canonical and versioned.

2025-10-28 — Quentin Harris (assignee): Drafted artifact layout proposal (model_slug/profile_id/version) and manifest fields. Open question: do we allow unknown fields for forward-compat? Current leaning: fail-closed for top-level, allow extension under "x_redwood" namespace only.

2025-11-02 — Marcus Lin (Security review): +1 to fail-closed. For signing, prefer detached signature over full blob signing to reduce re-upload churn. Also ensure publish endpoint writes an audit event with principal + source (CI vs human).

2025-11-07 — Arjun Desai: Please ensure we can attach eval/perf reports as artifacts (not required for runtime) so review tooling can link to a specific profile version. Also need sequence length regimes in manifest; we’re seeing different sweet spots for int4 on long-context.

2025-11-14 — Quentin Harris: Implemented schema validation + semver monotonicity checks in registry service. Added dry_run publish. Pushed PR 912 for layout + manifest; PR 931 for publish API + permissions.

2025-12-03 — Hiro Tanaka: Added requirement: manifest must include kernel constraints and min runtime version; we’ve already hit incompatibilities between sm80/sm90 kernels. Please enforce that constraints are present (even if broad) for int8/int4 profiles.

2025-12-05 — Quentin Harris: Updated validation to require kernel_constraints for quantized methods (int8/int4). fp16/bf16 profiles can omit. Added explicit hardware_scopes non-empty requirement. Tagged errors with JSON pointer paths.

2026-01-08 — Priyanka Bose: Ran a full publish in staging with a candidate int8 profile; validation errors were actionable. One tweak requested: include the accepted canonicalized manifest in response so we can store it in the eval publish PR artifacts.

2026-01-14 — Quentin Harris: Merged PR 912 + 931. Added response echo of canonical manifest (stringified JSON) for tooling. Marking Done; follow-ups tracked in ENG-18437 (runtime fetch) and ENG-18488 (eval harness attach).
